findings.evidence: HeegnerNumbers.lean:79 `def heegnerDiscriminants : Finset ℕ := {3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163}`; SmallDiscriminant.lean:66-70 rewrite `hD` into `mem_heegnerDiscriminants` via `simp`/`omega`.
findings.fix: State it as `{n : ℕ} (hn : NumberField.discr K = -n) (hmem : n ∈ heegnerDiscriminants) : classNumber K = 1`. If the ℤ-literal form is wanted for the final classification, derive it from the `heegnerDiscriminants` form, not the other way round.
findings.issue: `classNumber_eq_one_of_discr_mem` writes out `{-3, -4, -7, -8, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163} : Finset ℤ` by hand. This duplicates `TauCeti.heegnerDiscriminants`, and the proof immediately converts the literal back to that set with `omega`. Callers working from `n ∈ heegnerDiscriminants`, the form used by H1.3 and the H3.6 recovery step, must repeat the same case split.

findings.evidence: SmallDiscriminant.lean:84 and :97 hard-code the seven-element ℤ literal. HeegnerNumbers.lean:79 already defines the canonical set.
findings.fix: Phrase the right-hand side through `heegnerDiscriminants`, for example `NumberField.discr K = -n ∧ n ∈ heegnerDiscriminants` with `hn : discr K = -n`. Under the range hypothesis this is the same as membership in the seven-element set.
findings.issue: Same problem: `classNumber_eq_one_iff_of_neg_fifty_one_lt_discr` uses the ad hoc literal `{-3, -4, -7, -8, -11, -19, -43} : Finset ℤ`, which is exactly the elements of `heegnerDiscriminants` below 51. A consumer cannot combine it with `classNumber_eq_one_of_discr_mem` or `heegnerDiscriminants` without reproving the correspondence by hand.

summary: The two new theorems write out their discriminant sets as literal Finsets instead of using the existing `heegnerDiscriminants`, so the same nine-element set now has two forms and consumers need two different lemmas. The rest of the surface is fine: no compatibility leftovers and no exposed bodies.
